taxes.summary: His campaign site lists lower taxes for families and small businesses as a priority.
taxes.short: Supports lower taxes for families and small businesses.

abortion.summary: His campaign site lists reproductive healthcare and the right to choose as a priority.
abortion.short: Supports reproductive healthcare and the right to choose.

education.summary: His campaign site lists fair public education funding to prepare students, and keeping extremism and exclusion out of schools while keeping all books in school and community libraries, as priorities.
education.short: Supports public education funding; keeping all library books.

healthcare.summary: His campaign site lists expanded access to mental health care for children and adults as a priority.
healthcare.short: Supports expanded access to mental health care.

energy.summary: His campaign site, under a heading of economic development, lists safeguarding the area's natural beauty, wildlife, and rural way of life while opposing the construction of any new warehouses or data centers.
energy.short: Opposes new warehouses or data centers; safeguards natural areas.

economy.summary: On her official House page, Flood says she is committed to promoting policies that protect workers while enabling employers to sustain and grow their business operations, and that she works with local business owners and job creators to enhance the local economy.
economy.short: Says she promotes worker protections while helping employers grow.

taxes.summary: In a November 2025 statement, Flood said she could not support the $50.1 billion General Appropriations bill because its spending level is too high, warning that revenue growth is not keeping pace with spending and that the state faces a structural deficit without lasting fiscal reforms.
taxes.short: Opposed the $50.1 billion budget bill as too high.

abortion.summary: A local news account of the 2024 race reported that the Pennsylvania Pro-Life Federation gave Flood a leans pro-life rating, that she voted for a constitutional amendment package stating women have no guaranteed right to abortion, and that she voted for a bill requiring burial or cremation of fetal remains.
abortion.short: Rated leans pro-life; voted for a constitutional amendment.

education.summary: On her official House page, Flood says she is focused on securing funding for Pennsylvania's schools, colleges, universities, trade programs and other educational institutions to give students opportunities for learning and success.
education.short: Says she is focused on securing funding for schools.

healthcare.summary: On her official House page, Flood says she is committed to measures that stabilize health care costs to make care more affordable and to expanding access to mental health services.
healthcare.short: Says she supports stabilizing costs, expanding mental health access.

energy.summary: In a November 2025 statement, Flood said repealing Pennsylvania's participation in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative and advancing permitting reforms would lower electricity costs, create jobs, and reinvest revenue into the economy.
energy.short: Says repealing RGGI and permitting reform would lower electricity costs.

guns.summary: A local news account of the 2024 race reported that Flood voted against a ban on high-capacity weapons, supported concealed carry without a permit, and opposed ghost gun regulations.
guns.short: Voted against a weapons ban, ghost gun rules; backed permitless carry.
